W8. DEG Results Processing

Author

Eunji Ha

Published

July 31, 2026

1. Significance of DEG Results

DEG analysis and the Multiple Testing Problem

  • p-value: the probability of observing the result by chance under the null hypothesis (H₀: no difference between groups)
  • Multiple testing problem: testing 10,000 genes at p < 0.05 would yield ~500 spuriously significant results → dramatic increase in false positives

Multiple Testing Correction

  • Bonferroni: \(\alpha / n_{total}\) → too conservative
  • FDR (False Discovery Rate): \(FDR = \frac{FP}{FP + TP}\)

Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) Procedure

“Stricter for higher ranks, more lenient for lower ranks”

\[ FDR \leq \frac{n_{total} \cdot p_{cut}}{i} \leq \alpha(0.05) \]

\[ p_{cut} \leq \frac{i}{n_{total}} \cdot \alpha \]

  • adjusted p-value (padj) … (with cumulative minimum applied) \[ p \times \frac{n_{total}}{i} \]
# Manual implementation of the BH procedure
pvalues <- c(0.04, 0.001, 0.05, 0.0001, 0.2)
genes <- c("GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneC", "GeneD", "GeneE")
df <- data.frame(Gene = genes, P_raw = pvalues)
df <- df[order(df$P_raw), ]
m <- nrow(df)
alpha <- 0.05
df$Rank <- 1:m
df$BH_Threshold <- (df$Rank / m) * alpha
df$Pass <- df$P_raw <= df$BH_Threshold
df$padj_calc <- pmin(df$P_raw * (m / df$Rank), 1)
df$padj_final <- rev(cummin(rev(df$padj_calc)))

# Built-in R function
df$R_function <- p.adjust(df$P_raw, method = "BH")

Independent Filtering (DESeq2)

  • Low-count genes → difficult to achieve statistical significance
  • Pre-filtering → reduces total number of tests n → increases statistical power
  • Cases where padj is NA in DESeq2::results():
    1. Low-count gene (excluded by independent filtering)
    2. Outlier gene (based on Cook’s distance)

2. Visualization of DEG Results

Notedownload practice data

save the following files in data/ in your R project

File Link
dds_DESeq2.rds 📥 Download 
dds <- readRDS('data/dds_DESeq2.rds')
res <- results(dds, contrast = c("condition", "Tumor", "Normal"))

MA Plot (Global View)

  • X-axis: Mean Average (A), Y-axis: Log Ratio (M = log₂FC)
  • Check for data bias and LFC inflation in low-count genes
  • Should be symmetric around Y=0
  • apeglm::lfcShrink(): controls LFC in low-count genes (recommended)
# MA plot
plotMA(res, ylim = c(-10, 10), main = "Before Shrinkage")

# LFC shrinkage (apeglm)
library(apeglm)
resLFC <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "condition_Tumor_vs_Normal", type = "apeglm")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plotMA(res, main = "Before Shrinkage", ylim = c(-5, 5))
plotMA(resLFC, main = "After Shrinkage (Recommended)", ylim = c(-5, 5))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

Volcano Plot (Gene Selection)

  • X-axis: log₂(Fold Change), Y-axis: −log₁₀(adjusted p-value)
  • Identify genes with large |LFC| and low p-value
library(ggrepel)

res_df <- as.data.frame(resLFC) %>%
  rownames_to_column("gene_id") %>%
  mutate(is_significant = padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) > 1)

p_thr <- 0.05; lfc_thr <- 1
vol_data <- res_df %>%
  mutate(diffexpressed = case_when(
    log2FoldChange > lfc_thr & padj < p_thr ~ "UP",
    log2FoldChange < -lfc_thr & padj < p_thr ~ "DOWN",
    TRUE ~ "NO"
  ))

ggplot(vol_data, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj),
                     color = diffexpressed)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = "blue", "NO" = "grey", "UP" = "red")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-lfc_thr, lfc_thr), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(p_thr), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text_repel(data = head(arrange(vol_data, padj), 10),
                  aes(label = gene_id), color = "black") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Volcano Plot",
       x = "Log2 Fold Change", y = "-Log10 Adjusted P-value")

Heatmap (Pattern Inspection)

  • Visualize expression patterns of top significant genes
  • Inspect patterns between Case/Control and identify outlier samples
  • Apply vst/rlog transformation → z-score scaling
library(pheatmap)

vsd <- vst(dds, blind = FALSE)

# Top 20 DEGs
top_genes <- res_df %>%
  filter(padj < 0.05) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(log2FoldChange))) %>%
  head(20) %>%
  .$gene_id

mat <- assay(vsd)[top_genes, ]
df <- as.data.frame(colData(dds)[, c("gender", "condition")])

pheatmap(mat,
         scale = "row",            # z-score
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         annotation_col = df,
         cluster_cols = TRUE,
         main = "Top 20 DEGs Heatmap")

📝 W8 Assignment: Simple vs. Paired Model

1. Comparing the Number of DEGs

  • Simple model (~ condition): ~17,000 DEGs
  • Paired model (~ patient + condition): ~15,700 DEGs

From a variance decomposition perspective: the paired model accounts for patient effects separately, so patient variance that was incorrectly attributed to condition in the simple model is now partitioned out. As a result, some genes lose significance, but the remaining DEGs are more likely to reflect true biological signal.

2. Gold Standard Genes

Validate the change in p-values between models using known LUAD marker genes such as TOP2A, SFTPA1, SFTPB, SFTPC, and AGER.

3. Volcano Plot with Highlight

# Highlight specific genes
highlight_genes <- c("TOP2A", "SFTPA1", "SFTPB", "SFTPC", "AGER")
highlight_data <- vol_data %>% filter(gene_id %in% highlight_genes)

ggplot(vol_data, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj),
                     color = diffexpressed)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("DOWN" = "blue", "NO" = "grey", "UP" = "red")) +
  geom_point(data = highlight_data, color = "purple", size = 3) +
  geom_text_repel(data = highlight_data,
                  aes(label = gene_id), color = "purple") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Volcano Plot (Paired Model)",
       x = "Log2 Fold Change", y = "-Log10 Adjusted P-value")
